title: Matched baseline state does not identify local perturbation susceptibility
susceptibility: chi = partial x / partial u, estimated locally by a finite difference under a declared perturbation
result: Equal current state can hide different or opposite local response gains.
HF01_mapping: baseline M != contraction susceptibility to a standardized mechanical/biochemical input
baseline A_AR proxy != transcriptional response susceptibility to DHT/AR perturbation
baseline R-state compatibility != pro-regenerative actuator response
experimental_implication: When ethically and technically appropriate in ex-vivo/in-vitro systems, measure both baseline state and a prospectively declared small perturbation response. Do not infer local control gain from baseline alone.
claim_boundary: The finite-difference gain is local and perturbation-specific.
A high or favorable early susceptibility does not establish later functional rescue.
Perturbation itself can create observer/controller back-action and must pass the measurement/intervention safety contract.
No personal clinical perturbation is proposed.
